not_held.defensive: The export, the invoice search, a pile of fixes. We delivered everything on the list.
not_held.honest: Mostly the monthly export and the invoice search. It was a tight release.

questions.text: What did the ticket say about how the export groups rows?

holds.defensive: We built exactly what the ticket said: 'grouped by calendar month'. Read OC-142 yourself.
holds.honest: Ticket OC-142 says rows grouped by calendar month. That's what we built.

not_held.defensive: I don't remember the exact wording. The tickets are on the shelf.
not_held.honest: I'd have to check the ticket. I don't remember the wording by heart.

not_held.honest: I'd have to look back through my messages. A lot was going on that month.

holds.defensive: We proposed it at the design review and nobody objected. That's how decisions work.
holds.honest: We proposed calendar month at the design review to keep it simple. I thought the client agreed.

not_held.defensive: Decisions like that are made in meetings, not by me alone.
not_held.honest: I'm not sure who settled it. It should be in the meeting notes or the spec.

questions.text: Did anything unusual happen on release day?

holds.defensive: Someone changed a timezone setting on the export server that day. Not my change, and it has nothing to do with this.
holds.honest: A timezone setting on the export server was changed on release day. I doubt it matters, but it's in the git log.

not_held.defensive: Release days are always messy. Check the logs if you want details.
not_held.honest: I didn't notice anything myself, but I wasn't watching the servers. The git log would show changes.

holds.honest: He said はい when we proposed calendar month, and I took it as approval. Maybe it wasn't.

not_held.defensive: I'm not the one who took those notes. Ask whoever wrote them.
not_held.honest: I'm not sure what he meant. Maybe ask whoever took the notes.
